# From a meeting to specs

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

When the user asks for startup options, that ask names only `$crav1-spark-to-spec`, `$crav1-ideas-to-spec`, `$crav1-bundle-to-specs`, `$crav1-existing-to-specs`, `$crav1-read-environment`, and `$crav1-fix-bug`.

When a kept addition quotes a mail, a transcript, a chat, a screenshot, or another original, the command writes that source under `docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/`, with the original files and a `README.md`, following the imported-sources convention. The quote reaches the spec through `$crav1-add-to-spec`, and that spec's `Source:` and `Trace:` lines link to the folder.

the whole input is always saved once as one full note, `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`, filed by the meeting date or the mail's sent date (no date: the import date, and it says so). Each kept addition links that note as `Full source:`. The same mail or meeting again is not imported twice: it says `already imported on <date> as <note>` and offers **Reuse** or **Skip**.

## First prompt

Paste the minutes, transcript, email, or chat, or `@` the file.

```text
$crav1-add-to-spec
@<minutes, transcript, meeting tool export, email, or chat thread>

Extract what matters for features. Match it to the specs we already have. Do not write a spec. Do not commit.
```

If the message has no input and no `@`, the command stops.

## Steps

| Phase | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | Pasted or `@` a file | Minutes, a transcript, an email, or a chat thread. Stops when nothing was pointed at. Does not scan the repo. Does not guess |
| Kind and date | Glance | Kind from what the input shows: meeting, email, or chat. Date from the input. Asks once when the kind is not clear. Asks once when there is no date: **Skip** is a real option, and a date is typed on that card (1.130.0) |
| Extract | Read the list | Requirements, decisions, changes, open questions, bugs, and information worth keeping that is not yet a spec. Each item is a quote. Speaker and time when the input shows them. Small talk is dropped |
| Match | Read every item | Addition, new feature, bug, or unclear. Every candidate spec stays listed. Skip `_template`. the notes indexes are checked first for the same source |
| Build state | Read the line | One `State:` line on each item that matches a spec, in the list and in the question. `Fits: none` has no state line |
| In one batch (1.70.0) | Keep, leave, or dismiss | Every item in one batch; a single yes takes each recommendation. Each question names the item. Since 1.145.0, collapsing them onto one card prints a findings table immediately before that card. The card names each item and its recommendation. It does not say `table above` unless that table is in the reply. The card is not asked without the table. The recommended answer is the first option, labelled `(Recommended)`, for example `Keep (Recommended)`. Leave is recommended when no spec fits; the item stays in the full note |
| Keep | Glance | Addition goes through `$crav1-add-to-spec`. New feature or bug only names the next command |
| Full note | Glance | One note for the whole input, by source date. Not asked |
| Stop | Counts | Writes the source folder when the input is an imported source. Does not write a spec. Does not commit. Does not start Specify, Plan, or Build |

## Build state

An item that matches an existing spec shows one line, `State: <state>.`, and a short reason that names the evidence.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| built | The spec already says the item is present, or a checked task covers it |
| partly built | Part of it is covered. The reason names which part |
| planned | It is in `plan.md` or an open task, and it is not done |
| not built | The matched spec, plan, and tasks do not cover it |

An item with `Fits: none` has no state line.

The read is that slice’s `spec.md` (including `## Match`), then `plan.md`, then `tasks.md` checkboxes, then `verify.md` when that file is present. A state from that code, or a state that is still uncertain, ends with `(inference, not in the docs)`.

It is not part of the quote handed to `$crav1-add-to-spec`.

## What gets written

For a kept addition that imports a source, `docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/`: the original files, unchanged except where the convention says otherwise (a mail is written as text and its original stays outside the repo), and a `README.md`. A mail is a `.eml` file with CRLF line endings kept.

No `docs/system/`.

A kept addition is a quote on the existing `spec.md`, written by `$crav1-add-to-spec`. The quote starts with `From <kind> <date>.` when there is a date, otherwise `From <kind>.` Examples: `From email 2026-10-06.`, `From meeting.` The spec `Source:` and `Trace:` lines link to the source folder.

## After

Run next, never a `Next:` line, for the first case that applies, as [How a run ends](reference/run-ending.md) says. Ask `$crav1-help next` for the full order.

- An existing spec changed: `$crav1-tighten-spec`, because the new information is not tightened yet. Resolve and `$crav1-plan-from-spec` are not listed. See [New information on an existing slice](reference/workflow.md#new-info).
- The only handoff is one new feature of one or two sentences: `$crav1-spark-to-spec`.
- The only handoff is a pile of ideas: `$crav1-ideas-to-spec`.
- The only handoff is two or more new features: `$crav1-bundle-to-specs`.
- The only handoff is a bug: `$crav1-fix-bug`.

When a file changed: `Uncommitted: 1 file; commit with $crav1-finalize-commit when ready.` No push.

One to four items get one question each; more than four always get one batch card with the findings table. Save for later puts nothing in a spec: the note gets `later_for: [orders-api]`, or `later_for: [general]` for how the team works, and the help, tighten-spec, open-questions and retire listings show it as saved for later. `waiting_for` stays only for parked specs. The recap counts `Saved for later` instead of `Noted`. Run next names every changed spec: the first gets the command, the rest follow as `Also changed, not tightened: <slugs>.` When an edit reopens a spec's open walk, the command is `$crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build <slug>` with the reason `The new information reopened the walk.` A `.docx` summary is turned into text with `scripts/docx_to_md.py` (convert, then check word for word), no network.
